title: arXiv Trending Mathematics — October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart; this is an inferred notable-paper ordering, not a measured popularity ranking. Citation evidence for these very recent papers is limited, and claims are preprint claims rather than independently validated results unless noted.

sections.title: Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors prove that for every k ≥ 3 and n ≥ k−1, a family of subsets of [n] containing no k-sunflower has size at most 2^((1−1/(16k³))n), establishing an exponential saving below 2^n.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1 gives the stated explicit bound; the authors transfer a vector-sunflower bound to set families by a probabilistic block reduction.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Families are arbitrary subsets of the power set of an n-element ground set; the theorem's nonvacuous stated range is n ≥ k−1. It concerns the Erdős–Szemerédi problem, not the distinct uniform sunflower conjecture.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an arXiv preprint, not a peer-reviewed publication. The authors report a Lean verification, but this report has not independently checked that formalization or the mathematical proof.
sections.ranking_evidence: An IBS Discrete Mathematics Seminar devoted a talk to the result on 28 October; the claimed resolution also has broad extremal-combinatorics and polynomial-method relevance.

sections.title: Erdős-Hajnal for excluding paths
sections.abstract: The author proves that every path has the Erdős–Hajnal property, using a new Gyárfás-path argument with bookkeeping blockades and splitting paths.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.2 establishes the Erdős–Hajnal property for every finite path P_t; Theorem 1.3 also covers two families of subdivided-claw graphs.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: For each fixed t, every finite simple graph with no induced P_t contains a clique or stable set of size at least |G|^c_t for some c_t > 0. The full conjecture for arbitrary forbidden graphs is not claimed.
sections.unique_caveat: The general Erdős–Hajnal conjecture remains open beyond the graph families treated here; this is one author's preprint and the proof has not been independently assessed here.
sections.ranking_evidence: The preprint received a substantive October 20 revision, and its introduction records independent parallel work on the path case by a Google Research/DeepMind team.

sections.title: The Exact Overlaps Conjecture for Self-Similar Measures on the Real Line
sections.abstract: For finitely supported probability measures on contracting similarities of the real line, the authors claim the exact-overlaps dimension formula and a generalized entropy–Lyapunov formula, using a new entropy inequality for sums of independent random variables.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 states dim ν = min{1, h_μ/|χ_μ|} for the self-similar measure generated by a finitely supported probability measure on contracting similarities of R; Corollary 1.2 gives the corresponding set-dimension formula when there are no exact overlaps.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The proved theorem is one-dimensional, with finitely many contracting similarities and finite support. The entropy inequality relies on abelian addition.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper identifies higher-dimensional settings beyond its stated extension as unresolved; the dimension formula is an author-attributed preprint claim.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper spans dynamical systems and probability, and its introduction documents a separately announced result on the same formula while distinguishing this paper's stronger explicit entropy inequality.

sections.title: Certified Fourier rounding for the real Grothendieck inequality
sections.abstract: The author gives a computer-assisted proof that the real Grothendieck constant is strictly below 1.77987164, certifying a five-variable rounding construction with interval arithmetic, a Fourier coefficient calculation, and an explicit tail bound.
sections.claimed_result: The paper certifies K_G^R < 1.77987164 for all finite real matrices and arbitrary vector dimensions; its finite coefficient computation runs through degree 403 and the remaining coefficient sum is bounded analytically.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result is for the real Grothendieck constant and the standard finite-matrix/vector formulation; numerical inequalities are claimed with outward interval bounds and rational final comparisons.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a certified upper bound, not an exact evaluation or matching lower bound; the certificate has not been independently audited here.
sections.ranking_evidence: It supplies source code and an exact certificate as ancillary files, cross-lists functional analysis with numerical analysis, and tightens the upper endpoint in another October preprint on the same constant.

sections.title: Primal/Dual Method for the Grothendieck Constant
sections.abstract: The authors prove 1.773 ≤ K_G ≤ 1.7799 for the real Grothendieck constant, using a primal/dual search based on Hermite projection games and Krivine rounding followed by rigorous certification.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract gives the rigorous interval 1.773 ≤ K_G ≤ 1.7799; the heuristic estimate K_G ≈ 1.779 is not itself a theorem.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The bound concerns the real Grothendieck constant; the paper's primal/dual search uses AI tools, with numerical certificates asserted to be rigorous.
sections.unique_caveat: The estimate is not an exact value; the authors distinguish their heuristic point estimate from their certified bounds. The large certificate set remains a matter for independent checking.
sections.ranking_evidence: A concrete interval bound on a central constant in functional analysis and computational complexity, with a distinct October preprint subsequently reporting a slightly sharper certified upper endpoint.

sections.title: A Proof of the Koumandos--Ruscheweyh Conjecture
sections.abstract: The author claims the sharp subordination conjecture for every 0 < ρ ≤ 1 and every degree n, with parameter μ bounded by an explicitly defined optimal threshold ν(ρ); the remaining finite interval inequalities are certified by ball arithmetic.
sections.claimed_result: For each 0 < ρ ≤ 1, n ≥ 0, 0 < μ ≤ ν(ρ), and z in the unit disk, (1−z)^ρ s_n^μ(z) is subordinate to ((1+z)/(1−z))^ρ; the threshold is claimed optimal.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: s_n^μ(z) = Σ_{k=0}^n (μ)_k z^k/k!, and ν(ρ) is the unique root in (0,1] of the integral specified in the abstract. The domain is the open unit disk.
sections.unique_caveat: The finite numerical certification is part of the proof and depends on the supplied code and interval covers; this report has not rerun or independently checked those certificates.
sections.ranking_evidence: The October 5 revision adds sharp consequences for starlike functions and Gegenbauer sections; the paper supplies rational interval covers, source code, and alternative-formula verifiers.

sections.title: Optimal Reduced Representatives of Quadratic APN Permutations in Odd Dimension
sections.abstract: For every odd n ≥ 5, the author claims that each quadratic APN permutation of F_2^n can be linearly transformed so its reduced polynomial representative has a zero-free derivative and two-element nonempty fibres, yielding permutation-polynomial lifts over the corresponding Galois rings.
sections.claimed_result: For odd n ≥ 9 the existence argument is formalized in Lean; n=5,7 are handled by classifications and finite certificates. The paper says the property fails for n=3 and that no such quadratic APN permutations exist for even n.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The theorem concerns quadratic almost-perfect-nonlinear permutations over binary fields F_2^n, with odd-dimension restrictions and invertible binary-linear pre- and post-compositions.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction is dimension-restricted and does not give the asserted property in even dimensions or at n=3; the journal submission is not evidence of acceptance.
sections.ranking_evidence: It cross-lists number theory, cryptography, and information theory, includes code, finite certificates and a Lean 4 formalization, and states it has been submitted to IEEE Transactions on Information Theory.

sections.title: A short open space curve of unit width
sections.abstract: The authors construct a three-dimensional unit-width curve of length about 3.905124162243593 and prove it is a strict local minimum within their candidate family, using analytic estimates, interval arithmetic and a Lean formalization, while conjecturing it is globally minimizing.
sections.claimed_result: It identifies a strict local minimum of length 3.905124162243593… inside a constructed family of rectifiable continuous curves of unit width in R^3, and proves the candidate has unit width in every direction.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The minimizing claim is local to the specified candidate family; the unit-width condition is certified over all directions using analytic estimates plus interval arithmetic on a finite cover.
sections.unique_caveat: Global minimality is explicitly conjectured, not proved; the local result does not exclude a shorter curve outside the candidate family.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper combines metric and differential geometry with numerical certification and machine-checkable proof materials; it corrects a previously conjectured candidate and supplies programs and a formalization.
